pricing.rule: Each delivered call bills price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005. A pending/async ack or an unverifiable charged call (delivered:false, refundable:false) bills price_usd × 1.15 with no per-call fee; refunded calls, in-batch duplicates and failed runs bill $0. A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

comment.comment:
Just listened to a “would you rather paperhand vs roundtrip” debate, my subsequent thoughts: 

Having roundtripped 1.7m and realizing 6 fig gains/losses within the last month..obviously could’ve played things better but it’s a part of the game if you’re trying to make absolute life changing money. Transparently 1) I’m still up a bit 2) been thru this before…but with all things considered, I don’t feel as much pain as I feel like I should.

If you’re a high T man trying to provide for everyone you love, it is your duty to seize on opportunities. And the only way out is through, that includes taking L’s on the chin. It’s not fun having your deeply internalized conviction betray you. But when you know the game you’re playing, the spots you choose to be in, it’s easier to let things play out.

My situation now reminds me of playing my first high stakes poker game against a pro + some whales. Won big but wouldn’t have performed the way I did if I didn’t get my mind right. I was aware of my table image, had a good read on the players, and told myself the money is simply x amount of big blinds as a mental cue to not let my emotions stray me away from my game plan.

Everyone has different trading styles, personally I have a big risk appetite when I feel like I have good odds. I don’t claim to be the most wise, insightful, or even a “trader”, but I know many of you can relate to the psychological side of things as of late…good luck frens 🪐

comment.comment:
$ORBIO | The GPU Isn't the Business. Utilization Is. 🪐

Today, I want to look beyond Orbio Compute's technical launch and focus on something that matters enormously to my investment thesis.

The economics.

For months, @orbiodotso has been building an AI inference marketplace, connecting users, developers, and autonomous agents to computing resources.

Now the team is taking a different step: operating its own confidential compute infrastructure.

This creates a potentially important business opportunity.

Instead of depending entirely on third-party inference providers, Orbio can begin controlling more of the cost and delivery of its own AI services.

But here's the catch.
Running powerful GPUs isn't free.
Servers cost money whether they're processing thousands of requests or sitting idle.

So the real opportunity isn't simply offering cheaper inference.

It's attracting enough recurring demand to make every GPU economically productive.

Let's put the published pricing into perspective.

Orbio Compute's Private rates:
• $0.27 per million input tokens
• $1.10 per million output tokens

At a hypothetical 80/20 input-output mix:
• 1B billable tokens = approximately $436
• 10B billable tokens = approximately $4,360
• 100B billable tokens = approximately $43,600

These are illustrative customer charges, not profits, and exclude infrastructure costs.

Suddenly, the scale of the challenge becomes clear.

A successful AI infrastructure business needs enormous, recurring, paid usage and efficient hardware utilization.

And this is exactly where I'm watching Orbio's next phase.
Can the team attract developers who integrate the API into real applications?
Can private AI become a product customers pay for repeatedly?
Can Orbio keep its GPUs sufficiently utilized while maintaining competitive pricing?

And most importantly for investors:
How does that business success translate into sustainable economic value for $ORBIO?

The CREDIT ecosystem and ORBIO staking provide existing connections between the protocol and token holders. But we still need evidence of how demand from Orbio Compute strengthens that relationship.

I'm not assuming the answers are already positive.

But I like that the project is moving toward questions that serious infrastructure businesses must eventually answer.

A working model is a technological milestone.

A profitable, scalable inference business would be an entirely different achievement.

I'm still holding $ORBIO and watching this transition closely.

The long-term vision remains ambitious.

Now I want to see the unit economics that can support it. 🪐

Sources: Orbio Compute announcement, November 27, 2026; Orbio protocol documentation.
